name: Medlife Crisis (Dr. Rohin Francis)
shortDescription: A consultant cardiologist taking apart health claims — including the ones made by other doctors with larger audiences.
longDescription: Francis is a practising consultant cardiologist and a university researcher, and the channel's stated premise is that there is a great deal of bad science on YouTube. A hundred and nine of a hundred and seventy-three uploads run over eight minutes. The critical work is the reason to watch: a piece on two prominent medical figures selling unfounded claims, a careful treatment of testosterone therapy and cardiac risk, and a recurring argument that the lesson drawn publicly when an athlete dies is usually the wrong one. He is equally willing to turn it inward — videos on who should be blamed for medical complications, and on a patient who taught him humility, are about the limits of his own profession rather than someone else's. A sixty-seven-minute conversation between two cardiologists on avoiding a heart attack is the most directly useful thing here.
notFor: Anyone wanting a protocol. He is generally arguing that the confident version of a health claim is unsupported, which is useful and is not a plan. Humour is constant and will not suit everyone.

categories.why: The counterweight this subject most needs — a practising cardiologist examining what actually influences healthy lifespan and dismantling the confident claims sold around it.
categories.evidence: A 67-minute discussion between two cardiologists on avoiding a heart attack, a piece on prominent figures selling unfounded medical claims, a treatment of testosterone therapy and cardiac risk, and a recurring argument about the wrong lessons drawn when athletes die suddenly.

entryVideo.title: 2 cardiologists discuss how to avoid a heart attack
entryVideo.whyThisOne: The single largest determinant of how long most people live, discussed by two people who treat it — and notably free of the supplements and protocols the longevity genre is built on.

caveats: A critic rather than a guide: the output is mostly about why a claim does not hold, which is valuable and rarely actionable. Cardiology is his specialty and confidence outside it should be read accordingly.
